title: I gave an AI agent $100 in paper money and never touched it. 25 days later it's $423
author: TradeyAI-R
selftext:
I just told an AI Copilot I wanted to trade BTC. It suggested a few strategies, I picked a simple MACD one, and it built the agent and started trading on paper money. The whole thing was a normal conversation. I didn't write a single line of code.

**The results after 25 days**

* $100 → $423.49 (+323%), all realized
* 22 trades, only 36% winners
* A few big wins did almost all the work

**The trade that made it**

BTC dropped this week, and things got wild. My agent caught the move on its own. Yesterday it closed a short for +$230 in one trade. The log shows exactly why: the MACD histogram flipped from -48.5 to +10.2 on the hourly candle, so it closed. No guessing, no "AI vibes."

**The ugly part**

High risk, high reward. It runs 20x leverage with no stop loss, and at one point it was down 65% from its peak. This probably isn't the best strategy, but I'm curious to see how it holds up.

**What I learned**

I never stepped in manually. I just let the agent trade. It was paper money, but it followed real market data for 25 days, and I still felt every up and down. That's how I actually tested whether I'd trust this strategy.

I'm leaving it running exactly as it is, no changes. Let's see if the +323% holds or gets wiped out.

Would you have kept it running at -65%, or pulled the plug?

If you're curious, it's TradeyAI (I work there). Paper trading is completely free, so you can test your own strategy without risking a cent. Link in the comments. I'd love honest feedback if you try it.

comments.author: Ok_Map5721
comments.body:
nice screenshot, but at 20x with no stop, a \~5% move against you is a wiped account. a 65% drawdown means it got most of the way there before BTC dropped and one short bailed it out. that's not the strategy working, that's the market falling while you happened to be short at 20x.

also small detail on the screen: the agent was created on 2026-09-02, but this run is 25 days old. were there earlier runs before this one? if so, how did they end? that number tells you more than the +323%.

and for anyone thinking of trying it: read the privacy policy part the comment above quoted. a service that stores your strategies and exchange API keys is a big ask. if you ever connect one, use trade-only keys with withdrawals off and an IP whitelist.
